# Dev Catalog

> A curated, rated catalog of useful developer scripts, tools, and workflows. Every entry records where it came from, its license, the platforms it runs on, what it requires, and a curator rating.

Full metadata for every entry is in [catalog/index.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/catalog/index.json). Install steps by entry type are in the [install guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/skills/dev-catalog/references/install.md). Repository: https://github.com/alex-red/dev-catalog

Rubric (dev-v1): seven 0–4 grades weighted by practical value 25%, dependability 20%, ease of use 15%, safety and control 15%, adoption cost 10%, portability 10%, upkeep 5%; weighted total / 40 gives a score out of 10. Higher is better on every axis. Missing grades produce no score. See the [rating guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/docs/ratings.md). Within each section, complete ratings come first, then incomplete ones, then entries with blockers. Evidence: reviewed, used, tested. Select for fit first, and never let a high score clear a blocker. Read a script before running it.

## Scripts

- [Prune merged local Git branches](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/scripts/git-prune-merged/SCRIPT.md): A dry-run-first Bash script that lists local branches already merged into the default branch and deletes them on --delete. It finds the default branch from origin/HEAD and never touches the base, the current branch, or branches checked out in a worktree. Use when: Local branches have piled up after merged pull requests and you want to clear the ones that are safely merged without guessing. — id `git-prune-merged`, 8.6/10, evidence tested, platforms macos/linux, requires git, bash, tags git, branches, cleanup, original, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/scripts/git-prune-merged/entry.yaml)
- [Reclaim disk space from developer caches and build output](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/scripts/disk-reclaim/SCRIPT.md): An interactive Bash script that finds reclaimable space in package-manager caches, build output, idle projects' dependencies, Docker, temp dirs and the Trash, lists it by risk (safe, rebuild, review) with sizes, and deletes only the items you pick after confirmation. Deletion is limited to $HOME and your own temp files. Use when: A development machine is running low on disk and you want to see which caches, node_modules, build outputs and leftovers are worth clearing before deleting anything. — id `disk-reclaim`, 8.4/10, evidence tested, platforms macos/linux, requires bash, tags cleanup, disk-space, caches, cli, original, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/scripts/disk-reclaim/entry.yaml)

## Workflows

- [Find a regression with git bisect run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/workflows/git-bisect-regression/WORKFLOW.md): A step-by-step method for finding the commit that introduced a regression, using an automated check script with git bisect run. Covers exit-code semantics, skipping unbuildable commits, flaky checks, merge-heavy history, and keeping a record. Use when: Something worked in an older version and fails now, and reading recent diffs has not shown the cause. — id `git-bisect-regression`, 9.1/10, evidence reviewed, platforms any, requires git, tags git, debugging, regression, original, informed by https://git-scm.com/docs/git-bisect, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/workflows/git-bisect-regression/entry.yaml)

## Tools

- [ripgrep (rg) recursive search](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/tree/e89fff89ac9af12e8d4ce9d5fd07beb408ca730f): A fast recursive search CLI that respects .gitignore, skips hidden and binary files by default, and supports Rust and PCRE2 regexes, file-type filters, multiline search, and searching compressed files. A drop-in for most grep -r uses. Use when: You search codebases from the terminal and grep -r is slow or noisy with build output, vendored dependencies, or ignored files. — id `ripgrep`, 9.3/10, evidence reviewed, platforms macos/linux/windows, tags search, cli, linked from https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/tree/e89fff89ac9af12e8d4ce9d5fd07beb408ca730f, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/tools/ripgrep/entry.yaml)
